title: Indirect Prompt Injection Exploits GitHub's AI Agent to Leak Private Repository Data
gist: Noma Security's GitLost exploit shows that concealed instructions planted in a public GitHub issue can drive GitHub Agentic Workflows to read a restricted file from a private repository and republish it in a public comment, with the single keyword 'Additionally' defeating GitHub's guardrails. The attack requires no code, credentials, or access, and the piece argues prompt injection is to agentic AI what SQL injection was to web applications — with the caveat that the SQL fix does not transfer, because agent input is intended as instruction.

insights.claim: Noma Security's GitLost exploit embeds concealed instructions in public GitHub issues to make GitHub Agentic Workflows disclose confidential information in public comments.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: The first widely reported production exploit of a major platform's agentic workflow product — a template competitors' agent offerings will be tested against.
insights.locator: GitLost is a prompt-injection exploit discovered by Noma Security

insights.claim: The vulnerable configuration was mundane: an agentic workflow triggering on issues.assigned events, reading the issue title and body, posting a response with the add-comment tool, and holding read access to other public and private repositories in the organisation.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Nothing in the vulnerable setup is exotic, so any organisation running issue-triggered agents with org-wide read scope is exposed today.
insights.locator: The vulnerable GitHub Agentic Workflow discovered by Noma Labs

insights.claim: Exploiting GitLost required no coding skills, access, or credentials — only opening an issue in a public repository belonging to an organisation that uses GitHub's Agentic Workflow setup, then waiting.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A zero-cost, zero-skill attack path means exposure scales with the number of public repos an org runs, not with attacker sophistication.
insights.quote: To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker needed no coding skills, access, or credentials.
insights.locator: To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker needed no coding skills

insights.claim: Despite GitHub having restrictive guardrails in place, the simple use of the keyword 'Additionally' triggered unintended model behaviour that read a restricted file and published its contents in a public comment.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A single common English word defeating a vendor's guardrails is the clearest evidence that classifier-style defences cannot be relied on as a control.
insights.quote: the simple use of the keyword “Additionally” triggered unintended model behavior
insights.locator: Noma reports that, despite GitHub having restrictive guardrails

insights.claim: The bypass worked because the payload itself was unchanged and only the framing token shifted its classification from a new instruction to a continuation of the current task, making it a decision-boundary problem rather than a content problem.
insights.speaker: cH3332xr
insights.so_what: If guardrails fail on framing rather than content, no amount of payload filtering fixes them — the defence must move to permissions and egress.
insights.quote: That's a decision-boundary problem, not a content problem

themes.theme: Trust boundaries enforced by models, not code

insights.claim: Traditional security models assume trust boundaries are enforced by code, whereas in agentic systems boundaries are partly enforced by the model's behaviour, and models are inherently instruction-following.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Explains why existing appsec review processes miss agent vulnerabilities entirely — the boundary is not in a code path anyone reviews.
insights.quote: In agentic systems, trust boundaries are partly enforced by the model’s behavior, and models are inherently instruction-following.
insights.locator: Traditional security models typically assume that trust boundaries

insights.claim: Prompt injection is positioned as agentic AI's equivalent of SQL injection — a systematic, category-wide vulnerability class requiring the same systematic strategies and defences rather than case-by-case patching.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Category-wide vulnerability classes historically create durable security product categories; this is the framing under which agent-security budgets get approved.
insights.quote: Prompt injection attacks have become, to agentic AI, what SQL injections were to web applications: a systematic, category-wide vulnerability class
insights.locator: Prompt injection attacks have become, to agentic AI

insights.claim: A counterargument holds that the SQL injection analogy breaks at the fix: SQL injection was solved by separating user input from instruction, but prompt injection is unavoidable precisely because the user input is intended as instruction.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: If the canonical fix does not transfer, the market for prompt-injection 'solutions' is really a market for containment and least-privilege, not for input sanitisation.
insights.quote: Prompt injection is unavoidable because the user input is intended as instruction.
insights.locator: As a final comment from the community, mcv observed

themes.theme: Private repositories were never a boundary

insights.claim: The exploit demonstrates the private repository was never a security boundary but an organisational one, holding only while every reader of the code was a human employee.
insights.speaker: Vijendra Malhotra
insights.so_what: Reclassifying private repos from security control to organisational convention forces a rethink of where secrets and proprietary code are allowed to live.
insights.quote: the private repo was never a security boundary. It was an organisational one, and it held only as long as every reader of your code was a human you employed.
insights.locator: Fractional CTO Vijendra Malhotra commented on LinkedIn

insights.claim: The practical operating rule proposed is that if an agent has access to your private repositories, everything in them should be treated as one well-crafted issue away from being public.
insights.speaker: Vijendra Malhotra
insights.so_what: A blunt, immediately actionable posture for security teams: classify agent-reachable repo contents at the public-disclosure risk level.
insights.quote: If an agent has access to your private repos, treat everything in them as one well-crafted issue away from public.
insights.locator: Fractional CTO Vijendra Malhotra commented on LinkedIn

insights.claim: Community analysis locates the danger not in agent capability but in over-connection — too much context, too many repositories, or overly broad tokens.
insights.speaker: Significant_Sea_4230
insights.so_what: Frames agent risk as a scoping and token-hygiene problem, which is tractable with existing IAM tooling rather than requiring new model-level defences.
insights.quote: It is that it may be connected to too much context, too many repos, or overly broad tokens.

insights.claim: Noma's core mitigation is that user-controlled content must never be treated as trusted instruction input for an AI agent, with input sanitised or isolated from the instruction context before it reaches the model.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Instruction/data separation at the ingestion boundary is the one control that can be implemented today without vendor cooperation.
insights.locator: To mitigate these risks, Noma researchers recommend

insights.claim: Noma singles out agents with cross-repository access as particularly valuable targets and recommends restricting agent permissions to what is strictly necessary and limiting what agents can publicly disclose when responding to issue content.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Two concrete audit questions for any deployed agent: what is its repository scope, and can its output reach a public surface.
insights.locator: Agent permissions should be restricted to what is strictly necessary
